prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a sideswipe while changing lanes in Baytown, Texas, and has wrist fracture. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1179; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to do this recorded statement. Can you confirm you're giving this statement voluntarily and that it's being recorded?

A: Yes, I understand it's being recorded and I'm giving it willingly.

Q: Great. Can you walk me through what happened on the day of the accident?

A: I was driving on the main road in Baytown, heading toward the interchange. Traffic was moving slowly, so I decided to move from the right lane into the middle lane to get around a slower truck.

Q: Before you changed lanes, did you check your mirrors and look over your shoulder?

A: I checked the mirror and I saw the lane looked clear. I didn't turn my head fully to look over my shoulder, which I probably should have done.

Q: What happened next?

A: As I started drifting over, I heard a horn and then felt a bump on the driver's side. The other car was in my blind spot. It sideswiped my car and both of us pulled to the shoulder.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the contact?

A: No, I didn't see it until it was already beside me.

Q: How were you injured?

A: My car spun a little when we hit, and I grabbed the steering wheel hard with my left hand. I felt a sharp pain in my wrist right away. I was taken to the hospital and they told me it was fractured.

Q: Are you still receiving treatment for the wrist?

A: Yes, I have a cast right now and I have a follow-up appointment with an orthopedic specialist next week.

Q: Is there anything you'd like to add or correct in your statement?

A: No, I think that covers it. I'm willing to provide any additional records you need.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
